priorStories.headline: U.S. resumes missile warnings for Ukraine
priorStories.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States had restored intelligence sharing used to warn Ukraine about incoming Russian ballistic missiles after blocking it for several days.

President Donald Trump had previously said the United States never stopped sharing intelligence, leaving the duration and circumstances of any interruption disputed.

priorStories.headline: Drone attacks hit St. Petersburg oil sites
priorStories.body:
An overnight Ukrainian drone attack caused fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and other locations around St. Petersburg, according to Russian officials. The regional governor reported one person killed and five wounded.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses destroyed 1,015 drones across several regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea. That unusually large count was not independently verified, and the extent of damage or disruption at the oil facilities was not disclosed.

priorStories.headline: French protest arrests rise to 2,400
priorStories.body:
French authorities raised the number of arrests following Saturday’s nationwide protests from roughly 400 to at least 2,400.

President Emmanuel Macron condemned the rioting and looting in a televised address Sunday, blaming much of the violence on radical far-left groups. Police again used tear gas as demonstrators gathered in Paris.

priorStories.headline: U.S. extends deportation protection for two groups
priorStories.body:
The Department of Homeland Security said Ukrainians and Sudanese enrolled in Temporary Protected Status will remain protected from deportation while the government makes final decisions about their programs.

The protections, which had been scheduled to end Monday, cover tens of thousands of Ukrainians and hundreds of Sudanese nationals.

priorStories.headline: Canadian base fire kills four soldiers
priorStories.body:
Four Canadian soldiers were killed and 39 people were injured when a grass fire spread rapidly during live-fire training at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta. Nineteen of the injured were in critical condition.

Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland said officials had known about the fire for hours but believed it was sufficiently contained to continue training. After winds shifted, the flames traveled about one kilometer in 36 seconds. Investigators had not determined how the fire started.

candidates.summary: Australian independent federal lawmaker Helen Haines was critically injured when a sport utility vehicle struck her outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, during the afternoon. Police arrested the 43-year-old driver and found a knife inside the vehicle. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the collision as deliberate, while police said the motive remained under investigation.
candidates.title: Australian lawmaker critically injured in vehicle attack

candidates.summary: Twelve migrants, including an infant, died in two incidents involving speedboats near the Greek islands of Lesbos and Samos. Greek authorities said one boat collided with a coast guard vessel during a pursuit and another overturned after a sudden maneuver. Twenty-two people survived, searches continued, and two alleged smugglers were arrested. The circumstances of the collision off Lesbos remained under investigation.
candidates.title: Twelve migrants die near Greek islands

candidates.summary: The U.N. World Food Programme said funding shortages were forcing it to reduce planned monthly food or cash assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million. The agency said the cuts would leave about 500,000 people without monthly assistance while roughly two-thirds of Gaza's population remained acutely food insecure.
candidates.title: World Food Programme cuts Gaza assistance

candidates.summary: The Philippine foreign ministry summoned Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to object to remarks it said conveyed a threat to use force. Jing had said China would “easily win” a conflict between the countries while responding to criticism of Beijing's conduct in the disputed South China Sea. China maintained that it preferred peace.
candidates.title: Philippines summons Chinese ambassador over remarks

candidates.summary: Uber said it won dismissal of two linked British lawsuits valued at about £340 million that were brought by thousands of London black-cab drivers and two former private-hire companies. The claimants had alleged that Uber provided misleading information when obtaining its London private-hire operating license.
candidates.title: Uber wins dismissal of UK taxi lawsuits

candidates.summary: A Swedish appeals court convicted former national security adviser Henrik Landerholm of gross negligence in handling secret information, overturning his acquittal by a lower court. The case involved classified documents he left at a hotel in 2023. The court fined Landerholm 52,000 Swedish crowns; he had denied wrongdoing.
candidates.title: Swedish court convicts former security adviser

candidates.summary: Sweden's parliament speaker asked Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist to explore forming a new government and gave her one week to consult other parties. The move followed parliament's rejection of Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson's proposed minority government amid disagreements within the centre-left majority.
candidates.title: Centre Party leader asked to explore Swedish government

candidates.summary: France's central government asked some local authorities to impose partial curfews following weekend riots and looting. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu did not rule out a state of emergency but said localized measures were more appropriate for now and ruled out a blanket Paris curfew. The government did not specify which areas would impose curfews.
candidates.title: French government seeks localized curfews after riots

candidates.summary: An attack attributed by local authorities to Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis killed 53 people and injured 200 at a government security-forces training camp in Shabwa province. Local authority sources said three ballistic missiles struck during an exercise. Reuters said it verified video showing casualties at the site.
candidates.title: Houthi attack kills 53 at Yemen training camp

candidates.summary: Myanmar's military-backed government released rare photographs of detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi and said officials had delivered two books, a sealed envelope and a diplomatic communication from Britain's King Charles. The release documented uncommon foreign contact with Suu Kyi, whose access to outside visitors has been tightly restricted.
candidates.title: Myanmar releases rare photographs of Aung San Suu Kyi

candidates.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear former National Labor Relations Board member Gwynne Wilcox's challenge to President Donald Trump's January 2025 dismissal of her. The justices left intact a lower-court ruling that the firing was a valid exercise of presidential authority.
candidates.title: Supreme Court declines NLRB firing challenge

candidates.summary: Florida authorities secured a state arrest warrant for former Cuban President Raúl Castro on one count of conspiracy to commit first-degree murder in connection with Cuba's 1996 shootdown of two Brothers to the Rescue aircraft, which killed four people. Castro, who was federally indicted over the same incident in May, has not been tried, and the state charge remains an allegation.
candidates.title: Florida issues arrest warrant for Raúl Castro

candidates.summary: Japan launched its uncrewed Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft aboard an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center at 19:41 UTC. The mission is intended to study Mars's moons, collect at least 10 grams of material from Phobos and return the samples to Earth in 2031. If completed, it would be the first sample-return mission from the Martian system.
candidates.title: Japan launches Mars-moon sample-return mission

candidates.summary: Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines remained in critical condition after undergoing overnight surgery following Monday's deliberate vehicle attack in Wangaratta. ABC News confirmed that one leg was amputated. Officials said the vehicle struck Haines, reversed and hit her again before a bystander restrained the driver. Counterterrorism authorities were participating in the investigation, but police had not established a motive or filed charges.
candidates.title: Australian lawmaker loses leg after vehicle attack

candidates.summary: Paris police imposed an overnight curfew at Place de la République and in the Les Halles shopping district following weekend rioting and looting. Entry and presence were prohibited from 11 p.m. Monday to 6 a.m. Tuesday, with gatherings banned from 8 p.m. Authorities in Lille and several other northern cities also imposed temporary curfews on minors, as did Nice.
candidates.title: Paris imposes localized curfews after riots

candidates.summary: Shabwa Governor Awad al-Wazir raised the reported death toll from a Houthi attack on a government security-forces training camp to 58, with more than 200 injured and 14 missing. Local authority sources said three ballistic missiles struck the Al-Alam camp during a training exercise. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree acknowledged targeting the camp, which he described as Saudi-run.
candidates.title: Houthi attack kills 58 at Yemen training camp

candidates.summary: A collapse at an unlicensed gold mine in the rural Chambero area of Santa Bárbara de Iscuandé killed 14 people and injured seven, according to authorities in Colombia's Nariño department. Governor Luis Alfonso Escobar said search-and-rescue operations had concluded and called for faster formalization of small-scale and unlicensed mines to improve safety.
candidates.title: Colombia mine collapse kills 14

candidates.summary: The U.S. Justice Department announced federal charges against 28 lawful permanent residents in California, alleging offenses including fraudulent voter registration, voting by a noncitizen and false statements in naturalization proceedings. Eleven defendants were arrested Monday. The cases involve voting or registration in elections from 2002 through 2026; the complaints, indictments and information contain allegations, and the defendants are presumed innocent.
candidates.title: Justice Department charges 28 California residents with election crimes

candidates.summary: A Kenyan court convicted doomsday preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 associates of murdering 190 children and one adult in the Shakahola Forest. The court found that Mackenzie's followers were ordered to starve themselves and their children, with guards preventing victims from escaping or eating. More than 400 bodies have been recovered in the wider investigation. Sentencing was scheduled for November 6.
candidates.title: Kenyan starvation-cult leader convicted of 191 murders

candidates.summary: A Russian drone struck a central park in Nova Vodolaha in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, killing six people, including three children, according to Ukrainian officials. Fifteen people were injured, including seven children. The park was occupied by families at the time, and preliminary findings cited by regional prosecutors identified the weapon as a Geran-3 drone. Russia had not commented on the specific strike.
candidates.title: Drone strike on Ukrainian park kills six
